steps.content: On the first day of school, Raven insists on giving lessons in the new classrooms at first, but gives up the idea after being told by the construction workers that there are a lot of air pollutants in these newly renovated rooms.
The safety of the students is far more important than where they should be taught.
So Raven sets up tables and chairs in the playground outside the teaching building.
You look around at the children. They're of different ages. Some appear to be about eight or nine years old, while others seem to be about fifteen or sixteen years old.
Raven has the Sinner standing in the nearby shadows to thank for such a good turnout.
She's sent, albeit with mock reluctance, all the kids from the Homeless to the Academy.
You also see something else that pleases your heart.
An enrollment application form that bears a name written in large, crooked letters...
Hella.
But the applicant is not present. Maybe she's afraid of you? You can even imagine what she would say if she saw you here.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Hey, what are you doing here? You're not here to laugh at me, are you?
You smile, replace the applications, and weigh them down with a stone. Then you find a seat in the back row and sit down, as if you were a parent of one of the students.
Almost five minutes into the first class, and the podium remains unoccupied.
However, in the next instant, a dark shape rushes into the room and takes up its place behind the podium.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Sorry, sorry I'm late... I lost track of time while preparing the best teaching materials for my dear students.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Listen to me. You gotta stay calm, no matter what happens here. All right?
The students look at Raven with suspicion, not knowing what she's going to do.

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Miss, what's going to happen? Is it going to explode?
A bold student raises his hand and asks his question.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Well, how should I put it... I've prepared a surprise for you.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: An explosive surprise.
As if on cue, a black crow appears above a student's head, flapping its wings.
The crow circles around a few times, drops a stack of textbooks on the student's desk, and flies away.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Heh, rotten bird, showing off again.
The shadow in the corner complains, but it doesn't sound angry.
The students watch in awe as a group of crows swiftly complete the delivery of the textbooks.
Such an ostentatious way to have books delivered. But that's just Raven being Raven.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: All right, my dear students, let's get your first class at the Syndicate Academy started.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: My name is Raven, like the name of the black bird. Of course, you can call me by my other name if you prefer...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Raye.
The class proceeds smoothly. You listen with interest. Whether it's because Raven is well-prepared for the class or because she's using a textbook from Eastside, you're not sure.
Time flies, and it's time for the students' first history lesson.
Before the lesson starts, you run into Raven in the corridor, who is carrying a lesson plan.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: If I said I didn't make preparations, would you believe me?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I wouldn't.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: If I said I'm fully prepared?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I wouldn't either.
Raven chuckles.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Looks like we're getting more and more in sync with each other.
Raven walks up to the podium in long strides. You stand to the side, watching the goings-on in the playground.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: All right, my dear students, take out your history textbooks. Let's begin our first lesson on Syndican history.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: We won't start with the year N.F. 81 today, the year when Syndicate was created. Instead, we'll talk about the year you are most familiar with first.
Raven turns around, and draws a horizontal line with chalk on the blackboard to create a timeline.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: The year I'm talking about is N.F. 98, my dear students. Check your textbooks and tell me what happened that year.
Raven adds a dot on the timeline.
Raven closes her eyes and waits for the answer among the rustling of pages being turned.

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: Miss, there isn't anything written about that year in the book!

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Yeah, it's blank.
The few students who can read have flipped through the entire textbook without the help of a dictionary, but they can't find any major events recorded for the year N.F. 98.
Raven asks the students to sit down, turns the pages for a second, and makes a slightly exaggerated gesture.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ah, look at me, I must be getting old. How could I have misremembered the year?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: My mistake. Let me see...

steps.speaker: Student D
steps.content: Miss...
A hand goes up.

steps.speaker: Student D
steps.content: Miss, I know... what happened... I think I know, although it's not written here.
After the initial surprise, she looks at the student encouragingly.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Tell everybody what you know then, loudly.

steps.speaker: Student D
steps.content: Well, actually... I learned it from my older brother. He told me that there was a very powerful organization in Syndicate during that period, called...

steps.speaker: Student D
steps.content: Rustfire!
There is a stunned silence when the name is uttered.

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Did Rustfire exist back then?

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: Is he making this up?

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: I don't think he is. I heard that Donald joined the organization around that time...
Raven taps on the table to silence the students.
Then, with a flourish, she tears the blank page from the textbook, accompanied by a satisfying sound...
Raven lets go of the page. Carried by the wind, it flies away.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Well done. You've given an excellent answer.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: History is all about personal experiences. If some of you witnessed or experienced a particular event, then this particular event must have happened.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: If you don't agree with a certain written account, or if you have something to add to it, it's up to you to decide what to do about it. You can tear it off, if that's what you want to do.
You observe Raven's facial expressions closely, trying to figure out what she's up to.
Raven plows on with her questions.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: So, what significant event occurred in N.F. 103?

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: I know. The Eclipse Operation!

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Exactly. You found this piece of information fast. Good job. You can sit down now.
He doesn't.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: What's the matter, kid? You've given your answer. Why are you still standing?

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: Miss, there's nothing about Syndicate in this textbook. It's all about the city on the other side.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Oh? Really?

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: That year, my whole family was out of work. My dad, mom, sister, me... and my neighbors as well. But Rustfire came to our rescue.

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: Our family too!

steps.speaker: Student D
steps.content: Our family too!
Several students stand up, echoing him.
Raven smiles, tearing off another page from the textbook.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: So, what significant event occurred in N.F. 108?

steps.speaker: Student D
steps.content: The Reconstruction of Rustfire!

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: And the return of Syndican Hero Donald to Rustfire.

steps.speaker: Student D
steps.content: Wait a second. I heard he betrayed Rustfire.

steps.speaker: Student B
steps.content: You got it wrong. Donald was injured; he didn't betray Rustfire. And he got a cool nickname too, the Thunder Halberd!

Raven goes on to pick out a dozen more years. When she asks about the significant events of each year, she always gets answers from the students; some even offer their own opinions. They're eager to share what they know about this or that historical event.
The bell sounds for the end of the spirited discussion, with pages of paper floating in the Syndican sky. In the end, only the covers of the history textbook remain.
How do you like the surprise the children gave you?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Haha, you were right; they did deserve a chance. These students saved me. They're orphans, but they have hope for a bright future, even though they know the dark truth of the past.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: They're fully aware of the circumstances they're in, but they never complain. They all hope that their life history will be remembered by others.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: It delights me to know that the most bright flowers can be found amid fire and ashes. That makes it all worthwhile.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Everyone can see their future clearly, and the future of the West District has never been brighter.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: The past is in the past, however painful it has been. It's time for us to look forward to the future.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ah, but before we do any of that, can you reimburse me for the money I spent on the history textbooks?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I'm gonna write another set of textbooks and have a few hundred copies made. Would it be okay if I put the expenditure under your name, the honorary principal of the Syndicate Academy?

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: What class do we have tomorrow?

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: Have your head gone all muddy from spending too much time on math? It's poetry, of course.

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Right. Math is really difficult. I'm lucky to have Miss Lavina as my math teacher; she's very patient with me.

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: Both Miss Raye and Miss Lavina grew up in that era. I can't believe that they're able to give us lessons after experiencing those horrible things...

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Yeah... I want to become just like Miss Raye. Someone who searches for light in the darkness! It sounds so cool.

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: Give me a break. I don't want to go back to those days when we never had enough to eat.

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Hehe, just saying. Like Miss Raye said in class before, "To forget is akin to betrayal."

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: Only by remembering the painful days of the past will we know how to strive for a bright future!

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: By the way, do you know who that person sitting in the last row is? A friend of Miss Raye's?

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: More than just friends! I hear that the two of them always have meals together, and ride in the same car!

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Really? Are they... ouch!
Before he can finish his sentence, a piece of chalk hits him on the forehead.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: What were you two gossiping about over there?
The two naughty students are visibly shaken.

steps.speaker: Student A
steps.content: Cough... Miss Raye, we, uh, were just talking about how amazing you are!

steps.speaker: Student C
steps.content: Yes... we were.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Hehe... Is that so? Then you two recite "To the Future" to me.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: There will be punishment if you even make a mistake or miss a word. That's my proudest work after all.
In the land of Syndicate, I witness both hope and despair.
Indulging in darkness, yet searching for light.
Writing poems, and becoming a poem.
In honor of the flames rekindled amidst the rust,
the winds howling amidst the forest,
In honor of the birds fluttering their wings in the storm, the flowers blooming in the mud.
In honor of dreams...
In honor of hope...
In honor of...
...the future

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: I hear this poem isn't a finished product.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Is that true? And if it is, when are you going to finish it?
The leader of the Homeless steps out from the shadows and smiles at the teacher known for her unconventional teaching methods.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Oh, about that? I'll get around to it when I get around to it.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: There will be more tales about heroes in Syndicate in the future. That will certainly keep me busy.
